transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-08-19
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 47 minutes
Attendees: Samir (Redwood AE), Nina (Redwood SE), Jordan (Redwood SE), Oliver (Keystone InfoSec), Maya (Keystone Cloud), Rory (Keystone Legal), Priya (Keystone Platform)

Summary:
Quick scope-gap analysis to confirm whether Redwood's hosted and private deployment options meet Keystone's EU-only processing needs for PII/PHI-adjacent insurance claims, and to validate KMS custody options (BYOK vs Redwood-managed), sub-processor region mapping, and audit log retention for regulatory audits.

Topics covered:
- Region pinning / EU-only processing and exceptions
- KMS integration, BYOK, and escrow options
- Sub-processor list and cross-border subprocesses
- Audit trails, egress controls, and SSO/RBAC mapping
- SLA/contractual remediation and next steps

Transcript:
[00:00] Samir (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining, appreciate you carving out time. quick intro from our side, I'm Samir, I'll run the call. nina and jordan here — nina's our S-E on infra and kms stuff.
[00:18] Oliver (Keystone InfoSec): Thanks, Samir. we've got a tight window — regulators want proof of no egress outside EU for our EEA customer claims processing, plus we need to see key custody options.
[00:36] Nina (Redwood SE): Yeah totally. to level set, Redwood offers hosted API in regions, dedicated reserved capacity, and our private deployment which can be VPC peered or on-prem. for EU-only processing we usually recommend private or dedicated with region locking, but there are trade-offs.
[00:55] Rory (Keystone Legal): When you say "region locking" do you mean guaranteed data residency, like contractual obligation and technical enforcement? also curious about subprocessors and transfer mechanisms.
[01:12] Samir (Redwood AE): Good q. we do both: contractual clauses in the DPA for processing boundaries and technical controls — region affinity routing, VPC peering, and egress filters. we also have a sub-processor inventory. i'll share the up-to-date list after this call.
[01:30] Maya (Keystone Cloud): quick practical question — for models that rely on external third-party embeddings or telemetry, is there any hidden cross-border call back? we've seen other vendors phone home during patch ops.
[01:47] Nina (Redwood SE): we call out telemetry in our privacy docs; default is no external telemetry for private deployments. for hosted we have telemetry but it's region bounded for EEA tenants; caveat is some infra-level API calls go to control plane in us-west for account mgmt, but payloads can be blocked.
[02:05] Priya (Keystone Platform): can you be specific about the control plane? we need to understand metadata flow — do logs or model prompts ever transit US control-plane endpoints?
[02:22] Samir (Redwood AE): short answer: in hosted, account metadata may touch the control plane in the US for multi-region accounts, but for private we can route control plane traffic into customer VPC and restrict egress. i'll let nina deep-dive on logs.
[02:39] Nina (Redwood SE): sure — audit logs: we store request/response metadata per token usage. for private deployments logs can be shipped to customer-managed s3 or internal ELK in the EU. there's an option to disable storing full prompts if needed (redaction).
[02:59] Oliver (Keystone InfoSec): ok that helps. what's the retention policy and can we get immutable append-only logs for e-discovery?
[03:16] Nina (Redwood SE): default retention is 90 days on hosted; for enterprise we support custom retention and WORM-style retention in customer buckets. you can also integrate with your SIEM via syslog or our secure streaming hook.
[03:33] Rory (Keystone Legal): we need to see SOC 2 Type II reports and ISO attestation. do you have these and can they be scoped to the EU infra?
[03:48] Samir (Redwood AE): yes we have SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001. the attestation covers our control plane, not customer-managed on-prem instances. for private deployments, you'll get more control and we'll include the deploy manifest in the compliance pack.
[04:06] Oliver (Keystone InfoSec): KMS — the crux. we need BYOK where customer keys never leave HSM in EU. do you support HSM-backed keys in customer region?
[04:22] Nina (Redwood SE): absolutely. we support external KMS integrations: AWS KMS in eu-west-1, Google CMEK in eu-west-1, Azure Key Vault as well. two modes: 1) Redwood-managed keys in customer-region buckets, 2) customer BYOK — you keep key material in your KMS/HSM and we never store raw keys.
[04:43] Maya (Keystone Cloud): what about ephemeral keys for model cache encryption? some inference runtimes use KV caches that persist across calls. are those encrypted under the same key?
[04:58] Nina (Redwood SE): K-V cache, yeah — our runtime encrypts KV cache at rest and the master key is from the configured KMS. with BYOK you control rotation, and we integrate key rotation hooks so cache re-encryption is orchestrated. sometimes the transcript mislabels it as K-V, so apologies earlier if that was confusing.
[05:20] Priya (Keystone Platform): escrow? we've been asked by compliance to consider KMS escrow for legal hold scenarios. does Redwood offer key escrow or custody services?
[05:34] Samir (Redwood AE): we don't hold customer keys. for escrow there are partner services — typically customers use a third-party escrow or nested HSM escrow that we can accept a wrapped key from. we can support KMS export wrapped under your HSM. we'll detail patterns in the KMS guide.
[05:52] Oliver (Keystone InfoSec): is there an option to deploy the inference runtime inside our AWS account so keys never leave and traffic never exits the VPC?
[06:07] Nina (Redwood SE): yes that's our private deployment model — runtime runs in customer VPC; we ship an image and orchestrate via terraform/helm. network egress is under your control. you'll still have the Redwood control plane for updates unless you opt for air-gapped on-prem where we provide an image and offline patches.
[06:28] Rory (Keystone Legal): ok on subprocessors — can you map who in the sub-processor list has data centers in US vs EU? we need to prove no US-based sub-processor touches EEA data.
[06:43] Samir (Redwood AE): we can provide a matrix mapping sub-processors to regions and function. note some third-parties provide CDN or DDoS mitigation which may have cross-border presence but not content access; we'll annotate access types.
[07:02] Maya (Keystone Cloud): question about lawful transfers — do you rely on standard contractual clauses (SCCs) or do you have other transfer mechanisms? post-Schrems II we need a concrete mapping.
[07:19] Nina (Redwood SE): SCCs are part of our DPA for cross-border transfers, plus technical safeguards: region pinning, encryption in transit and at rest, and refusal of export of plaintext. we'll also provide our DPIA summary.
[07:35] Priya (Keystone Platform): any customers using your hosted EU region that still require zero metadata leaving EU? how do you technically isolate metadata?
[07:50] Samir (Redwood AE): metadata isolation is tricky on multi-tenant hosted systems. for strict requirements we recommend dedicated or private. with dedicated you get tenant-isolated GPU pools and control plane affinity to EU region.
[08:08] Oliver (Keystone InfoSec): can we get a flow diagram of control plane interactions, including auth token exchange, so our architecture team can run threat modelling?
[08:23] Samir (Redwood AE): yes, action item for me — i'll drop a control-plane/data-plane diagram and call out which endpoints are US vs EU.
[08:34] Jordan (Redwood SE): adding: auth uses signed JWTs with short-lived tokens. SSO is supported via SAML/OIDC, and we map IdP groups to internal RBAC roles. we can also sync SCIM for user provisioning.
[08:52] Rory (Keystone Legal): for audit purposes we need admin role separation — can you show RBAC matrix and prove logs of admin actions are immutable?
[09:06] Nina (Redwood SE): RBAC is role-based with admin/ops/audit roles. admin actions are logged; for private we can ship logs to your WORM bucket. for hosted we maintain tamper-evident logs with HMAC and append-only sequences. transcription note: sometimes our tooling says "H-M-A-C" in the logs; it's HMAC.
[09:27] Priya (Keystone Platform): performance question — if we pin region and use BYOK with customer KMS in eu-west-1, what's latency and any throughput hit from key encryption ops?
[09:44] Jordan (Redwood SE): minimal — keys are used to wrap DEKs (data encryption keys), runtime uses local DEK for fast crypto ops. KMS calls are mostly on rotation/unwrap on startup; normal token path doesn't call KMS per request.
[09:59] Oliver (Keystone InfoSec): good. any pitfalls we should be aware of during onboarding? like certain features that force cross-border processing?
[10:12] Nina (Redwood SE): two things: 1) some telemetry and billing metadata may hit our global control plane unless routed into customer VPC; 2) model fine-tuning in hosted mode might go to shared infra — for EU-only, prefer private/dedicated and disable hosted fine-tune.
[10:30] Samir (Redwood AE): also worth noting third-party model runners like some Llama forks call home for certain ops; when we onboard a model we document external dependencies.
[10:42] Rory (Keystone Legal): can you confirm you can contractually commit to region locking? we need language for our legal team that prevents data export except on explicit exception.
[10:56] Samir (Redwood AE): yes we offer DPA addenda with region restrictions and we can add penalty/escrow clauses for breaches. we'll have legal follow up to draft terms.
[11:10] Maya (Keystone Cloud): about patching windows — if runtime needs urgent critical patch, how do you apply it on private air-gapped? we need SLA on security patches.
[11:24] Nina (Redwood SE): for air-gapped/airgapped we provide offline patch bundles; customers schedule maintenance windows and apply them via our installer. for managed private we orchestrate patches with your approval; SLA for critical patches is defined in enterprise contract.
[11:40] Priya (Keystone Platform): for our internal change control we'll want proof of patch integrity — signed packages, checksums, and repo attestations.
[11:52] Jordan (Redwood SE): packages are signed; we provide PGP signatures and checksums. we also publish SBOM for runtime components.
[12:06] Oliver (Keystone InfoSec): ok, walk me through an example: keystone wants EU-only processing for claims. user uploads PDF, model generates extraction, writes back to our DB in eu-west-1. what's the end-to-end flow and where could data leak?
[12:24] Nina (Redwood SE): e2e flow: 1) client uploads to keystone s3 eu bucket -> 2) request routed to private runtime in your VPC (eu) -> 3) runtime pulls model weights that are staged in eu artifact store -> 4) KMS unwrap happens via your KMS in eu -> 5) inference executes locally, results posted back to your DB in eu. leak points: any external connectors (email, third-party lookups) or misconfigured egress ACLs.
[12:50] Samir (Redwood AE): also logs — make sure prompts are redacted or logs stored in your controlled bucket.
[13:01] Rory (Keystone Legal): we'll need a written attestation of those e2e guarantees for our auditors.
[13:10] Samir (Redwood AE): we can provide an attestation letter scoped to private deployment and dedicated contracts.
[13:18] Maya (Keystone Cloud): about subprocessors — in your matrix, are there any US-based monitoring vendors that have read access to payloads? we need explicit no-read clauses.
[13:33] Samir (Redwood AE): we will annotate the list. most infra subprocessors (CDN, DDoS service) have metadata-only access, not payload; we will flag any with potential payload access.
[13:45] Oliver (Keystone InfoSec): regarding SSO — can we federate via our IdP and have group-based roles enforced? and is SCIM supported for deprovisioning?
[13:59] Jordan (Redwood SE): yes SAML/OIDC works; role mapping via groups, and SCIM provisioning supported for user lifecycle. we recommend just-in-time provisioning for lower blast radius.
[14:12] Priya (Keystone Platform): is there a way to get a sandbox private deployment for tests — we want to run artifacts and validate no egress.
[14:25] Nina (Redwood SE): yes we offer a short pilot private deployment — typically 2-4 weeks — we can scope a limited environment with 1 rack equivalent, EU-only, and provide a test plan to validate egress.
[14:40] Samir (Redwood AE): great, next steps recap in a moment. quick clarifying Q — any regulatory nuance? GDPR DPA clauses we should be aware of?
[14:50] Rory (Keystone Legal): Schrems II follow-up docs, evidence of technical controls, and sub-processor mapping for audits. also we may ask for a contractual carve-out around lawful requests — we need transparency.
[15:05] Nina (Redwood SE): we have a lawful request process; we notify customers unless prohibited. for private on-prem you control that entirely.
[15:17] Oliver (Keystone InfoSec): would like to see a sample DPA with region-locking language to run by our counsel.
[15:27] Samir (Redwood AE): action: i'll send sample DPA + SOC2 + sub-processor matrix. nina will share KMS patterns and pilot proposal.
[15:36] Jordan (Redwood SE): also we'll include terraform/helm snippets and a runbook for private deploy so your platform team can smoke test.
[15:45] Priya (Keystone Platform): good — and we'll prepare a list of EU-only systems and confirm which datasets are in scope.
[15:53] Rory (Keystone Legal): finalize week-of meeting with our security and legal — prefer 2027-08-30.
[16:01] Samir (Redwood AE): noted — we'll pencil that in. thanks everyone.

End of meeting.
